comments.text: Over the last year- and having witnessed the seeming sigmoidal nature of the scaling laws, has had me wondering if this is something Google was already very aware of. Perhaps there is a true "low" ceiling to upper capabilities of traditionally trained LLMs. It may be that we require DeepMinds zero shot approach to truly ascend the slowing scaling laws we're witnessing in other domains. Btw, IMHO, test time adaptations (TTA, sometimes called TTT, training) would preference a zero shot model over one with an already highly compressed corpus of pre trained knowledge. I think we'll utilize a tick tock model, LLMs today are like highly efficient compression algorithms for large amounts of data, i.e. memory. DeepMinds approach meanwhile will likely better fit the niche of de novo knowledge gathering. Crazy times all
